notes.summary: BJ v4 already constructs the genuine singular finite-energy operator with raw mass V, intrinsic dual-energy targets, comparison and uniqueness. Its existence theorem remains conditional on EP.
notes.detailedSummary: The primary-source scope includes reduced nonnormal projective varieties over algebraically closed trivially valued fields. In the retained characteristic-zero, integral, ample-line-bundle domain, the raw operator has mass V=(L^n), finite dual energy is equivalent to integrability of every E1 potential, and uniqueness modulo constants and domination precede envelopes. Actual variational attainment uses EP compactness and bounded-J target integration continuity. The new Wu singular EP claim is not accepted by citation.
notes.text:
Primary-source partial theorem. Let k be algebraically closed, trivially valued and characteristic zero; X reduced irreducible projective; L ample; omega=c1(L), n=dim X and V=(L^n)>0. No normality or measure-support restriction is used in the following operator, target condition or uniqueness assertions. This retains the original geometrically unibranch equation domain but does not prove existence on it.

BJ means reduced, possibly nonnormal varieties at LF450–469 and resumes general projective varieties at LF3649–3658. Its test configurations are closed integrally INSIDE THE PRESCRIBED GENERIC FIBER (Definition1.10 and Theorem1.13, LF759–849), rather than absolutely normalized. The polar-ideal determinant trick forces associated vertical poles to be DVRs; vertical depth two excludes higher-codimension poles. This preserves a nonnormal generic fiber. On a common relative closure the actual raw mixed model measure is sum_E b_E product_i((theta_i,model+D_i)|E) delta_vE, with b_E=ord_E(t)>0 and v_E=b_E^(-1)ord_E|k(X). Nef restrictions give nonnegative weights; the central fundamental cycle and rational equivalence to the generic fiber give mass (theta_1…theta_n)_X, including all b_E factors.

The compactified symmetric intersection pairing is determination-independent by projection formula and translation adds c times the other classes' mixed degree. Extend it by infimum over model majorants. Monotonicity is intersection positivity. For upper semicontinuity select a majorant tuple below a strict pairing threshold; continuity of sup(phi_i−psi_i) gives nearby translated majorants, and the translation rule bounds the error. Decreasing-net continuity follows. Mixed energy bounds extend it multilinearly to finite-energy differences. Define E(phi)=pairing((omega,phi)^(n+1))/((n+1)V), E(0)=0, E(phi+c)=E(phi)+c, and E1={genuine omega-PSH phi:E(phi)>−infinity}. Pairing with (0,a), for actual algebraic PL tests, defines integration. Positivity bounds its norm by mass times ||a||, PL density and Radon representation give the genuine mixed measure (BJ7.18–7.19 LF3980–4057), with exact mass, model agreement, mixed integrability and decreasing continuity. Probability MA=raw MA/V.

Weighted7.21 has an explicit sign correction: integral phi_0 dM equals the pairing containing phi_0 MINUS the zero-test pairing, as correctly printed LF4107–4113; LF4119–4123 reverse these terms. Both corrected pairings converge; translate below zero and apply the positive weighted-measure lemma to the negative test. Model winning-component equality then passes to E1 using weighted continuity separately for max(phi_j,psi_j) and psi_j. Their difference need not decrease. Thus 1_{phi>psi} MA(max(phi,psi))=1_{phi>psi} MA(phi). Displaced maxima and equal masses give integral_{phi<psi} MA(psi)<=integral_{phi<psi} MA(phi). This repairs the last citation LF4585 without assuming measure monotonicity.

For I(phi,psi)=integral(phi−psi)(MA(psi)−MA(phi)), mixed negativity gives I>=0. BJ10.3 separation with finite-energy divisorial Diracs and the trivial Dirac forces equal divisorial values when I=0 and suprema agree. Divisorial determination gives equality everywhere: actual Corollary10.4 LF5444–5456. Equal measures imply one additive real constant. Actual Corollary10.6 LF5468–5477 proves domination before EP: replace phi by max(phi,psi) under phi<=psi MA(psi)-a.e.; the replacement has nonpositive I with psi, hence a constant difference; a.e. equality removes the constant.

A raw target nu is positive Radon with mass V. For mu=nu/V its exact intrinsic condition is E^vee(mu)=sup_{psi in E1}(E(psi)−integral psi dmu)<infinity. BJ9.20 LF5266–5301 equates this with integrability of EVERY E1 potential on integral X. Proof mechanism: if integration were unbounded below on normalized J=−E<=C, select psi_j with integrals <=−2^j. The decreasing convex sums sum_{j<=m}2^(−j)psi_j have energy >=−C and converge to an E1 potential with integral −infinity, contradiction. Mixed expansion gives J(tpsi)<=C_n t^2J(psi); scaling then gives −integral psi<=A sqrt(J)+B and finite dual energy. Actual outputs satisfy the condition by mixed integrability and the concave tangent inequality. No support restriction enters.

Actual BJ8.5 LF4843–4960 gives the unconditional outer expansion E-down(phi+tf)=E(phi)+t integral f MA(phi)+O_f(t^2), uniform in phi, for PL f. Its mixed degrees bound the error; both signs and uniform PL approximation give continuous directions. The upper endpoint in the printed LF4954 squeeze must be integral f_m MA+epsilon_m, not minus epsilon_m. For unbounded phi, identification with energy of the genuine envelope requires EP. BJ's relative-volume inputs cited outside the ten caches are used through its published theorem, not independently reproved here.

Under genuine EP, BJ5.11 LF2819–2842 proves normalized-PSH compactness by bounded divisorial evaluations, Tychonoff, genuine tail upper envelopes and divisorial nonnegligibility. A dual maximizing sequence has bounded J by9.15. A weak subnet has finite energy by J-lsc;9.19 LF5245–5262 supplies L1(mu) convergence via uniform bounded-J approximation by integrations against maximizing model MA measures, before attainment. Its scalar identity is |a−b|=2max(a,b)−a−b, correcting LF5254. Energy usc yields an ACTUAL maximizer. Both signs in outer differentiation and duality give the genuine equation. The raw objective VE−integral phi dnu is translation invariant exactly at mass V.

Consequently every intrinsic target has a unique-modulo-constants genuine solution IF EP holds. Actual BJ12.8 LF6092–6141 equates EP, onto MA and E1 completeness;12.9 LF6144–6146 is the smooth sufficient endpoint. Operator construction and strict concavity do not establish singular EP. Dimension zero is immediate (one point, V=1, E(c)=c).

notes.summary: New explicit extended-coordinate strict barriers and genuine AFS approximants, including individual floors for real supports; original-ring hull localization is proved using actual normalization pole orders.
notes.detailedSummary: The soft maximum has a unique strict support and a uniform gap off every neighborhood, even at infinite coordinates. Multinomial approximants are globally uniform and retain actual generators. Real coefficients use individual logarithm floors and nested rational intervals. A countable-field strict potential has an explicit decreasing diagonal. Localization uses finite normalization only for orders, integrality of h^p f^q, and one f^N annihilator in the original ring. Limit hull comparison still requires controlled approximation.
notes.text:
Independent proof drafts, with n1 fixing the meaning of the genuine global cone. Work over the retained algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero k. Actual rational affine FS (AFS) means max(lambda,c_i log|f_i|+C_i), rational constants and positive rational c_i, with the list containing algebra generators of the ORIGINAL affine ring. Positive rational sums and maxima are AFS after distributing maxima; floors in the other factors retain generator branches. A power branch can be supplemented identically by a low branch of the original generator, since for 0<eta<c a sufficiently large M gives eta log|z|−M<=max(lambda,c log|z|+C) at all norms, including zero. Upper growth always means u<=H+C. The auxiliary contact inequality uses b(s)>=ell(s)+C and equality at t with the same C. These definitions do not redefine genuine PSH.

For T_N=(R union {+infinity})^N choose integer a>=log(N+1) and chi(t)=a^(−1)log(1+sum exp(−a t_i)), with exp(−a infinity)=0. It is continuous and lies between max(0,−t_i) and that maximum+1. At t let I be its finite coordinates, Z=1+sum_I exp(−a t_i), p_0=1/Z and p_i=exp(−a t_i)/Z. The support ell_t(s)=chi(t)−sum_I p_i(s_i−t_i) has zero coefficients at infinite coordinates and is −infinity if a used coordinate becomes infinite. Convexity gives chi>=ell; the Hessian a(diag p−pp^T) is positive definite since p_0>0, and any new finite coordinate formerly at infinity strictly increases chi. Equality occurs only at t.

For the full uniform gap, chi(s)−ell(s)>=max(0,−s_i:i in I)+sum_I p_i s_i−C_t. The homogeneous part is positive on every nonzero vector because the weighted average of 0,−s_i, with ALL positive weights p_0,p_i, is strictly below their maximum unless they all vanish. Compactness of the unit sphere gives coercivity. A bounded gap sublevel confines these coordinates to bounded intervals; bounded chi and ell then bound the other coordinates below, with their infinity endpoints allowed. These are closed compact sublevels of the extended product, and their only zero is t. Taking a minimum outside any neighborhood of t, and using the sublevel bound outside that compact set, proves a uniform positive gap there. For I empty, chi directly bounds all coordinates below and the same argument applies.

For z_0=1,z_i=exp(−at_i), the multinomial expansion has B_m=binom(m+N,N) nonnegative terms. Their maximum lies between (sum z_i)^m/B_m and (sum z_i)^m. Hence q_m=max_{|beta|=m}{−sum_{i>0}(beta_i/m)t_i+log binom(m;beta)/(am)} obeys q_m<=chi<=q_m+log(B_m)/(am) on the ENTIRE extended product. At poles those terms are −infinity, but beta_0=m gives a zero floor. After t_i=−log|f_i|, every term is (1/m)log|product f_i^beta_i| plus its intercept; beta_i=1,beta_0=m−1 retains each actual generator. Choose m_j with error<=epsilon_j/4, round intercepts upward with error<=epsilon_j/4 and add rational epsilon_j, epsilon_{j+1}<=epsilon_j/4. Values lie between chi+3epsilon_j/4 and chi+5epsilon_j/4, so these actual AFS functions decrease globally and converge uniformly to chi.

For a real support sum p_i log|f_i|+C, omit zero coefficients. Choose rational AFS H>=1 including the original generators and integers D_i>=1 with log|f_i|<=D_iH. Set F_ij=max(log|f_i|,2^(−j)H−j). They are AFS, decrease to the individual logs including poles, and F_ij<=D_iH. Choose nested rational intervals 0<=q_ij<=p_i<=r_ij with q increasing and r decreasing to p_i, and rational C_j decreasing to C. Let eta_j=sum D_i(r_ij−q_ij) and L_j=sum q_ij F_ij+(eta_j+2^(−j))H+C_j. The coefficient error costs at most eta_j H; negative logs improve the lower-bound inequality, so L_j majorizes the support. Moreover eta_j−eta_{j+1}>=sum D_i(q_i,j+1−q_ij). Expanding L_j−L_{j+1}, use F_ij>=F_i,j+1 and F_i,j+1<=D_iH to get nonnegativity. The positive 2^(−j)H and the INDIVIDUAL floors retain original generator growth. At a zero of f_i with p_i>0, q_ij is eventually positive and q_ij F_ij tends to −infinity, while all other terms are bounded above at that point. Thus the limit is exact on the support's pole set as well. Flooring only the whole sum fails: on A2_{z,w}, max(p log|z|,−j)=−j along z=0 as |w| tends to infinity, so it cannot retain a positive w-generator branch.

For countable k, enumerate the affine ring, retaining generators in each finite tropicalization. Those maps generate the topology. Degree bounds give rational gamma_j>0 with 0<=gamma_j chi_j<=2^(−j)(H+1). The sum rho is continuous locally uniformly and of upper logarithmic growth. T_r=sum_{j<=r}gamma_j chi_j+2^(−r)(H+1) decreases. Approximate its finite continuous sum uniformly globally by AFS A_r with errors epsilon_r=4^(−r); adding B_r=2sum_{i>=r}epsilon_i gives a decreasing sequence since the consecutive difference is >=epsilon_r−epsilon_{r+1}>0. For a neighborhood B of x, replace one finite tropical chi term by its support at x. The resulting rho-prime equals rho at x, is <=rho, and <=rho−delta outside B. To regularize it, approximate that ONE support by the decreasing L_r above, the other finite continuous terms uniformly, retain the same decreasing tail and add B_r. The decreasing support and uniform error shifts prove monotonicity; bounded other terms prove the exact −infinity limit on its divisor. No uniform approximation at logarithmic poles or singular EP is used. This countable construction is not arbitrary-cardinality EP.

Original-ring pole-order localization: let A be integral affine, f nonzero, h in A_f, U actual AFS on Spec A, and a log|h|+b<=max(U,−c log|f|)+C on Y_f, with a,c>0. On a height-one divisor D of the finite normalization, regular elements of A have nonnegative orders. Evaluating on rays r ord_D and dividing by r gives a max(−ord_D h,0)<=c ord_D f. For positive integers p,q with q/p>c/a, z=h^p f^q therefore has no height-one poles and lies in the normalization; it is integral over A and also in A_f. The finite module A[z]/A vanishes after inverting f, so ONE f^N kills it. Thus f^N z^l=f^(N+ql)h^(pl) belongs to the ORIGINAL A for every l>=1.

For compact L in Y_f and x in its ORIGINAL A-polynomial hull also in Y_f, take |log|f||<=M on L union {x}. Apply the hull inequalities to these regular polynomials, divide by pl, let l tend to infinity, then q/p decrease to c/a. This gives a log|h(x)|+b<=sup_L(a log|h|+b)+2cM. If h(x)=0 it is immediate; if h vanishes on L, the same tests force h(x)=0 because f(x) is nonzero. No normalization hull or subtraction of infinities is used. Denominator counting is false already for f=z^2,h=z^(−1)=z/f,a=2,c=1: the original growth bound holds with U=max(0,2log|z|), but a times denominator exponent1<=c fails. Actual orders give 2 times1=1 times2.

For already regularizable v on Y_f with upper growth U+C, IF controlled approximants w_i decreasing to v satisfy w_i<=2max(U,−epsilon log|f|)+B_i, apply the proved inequality branchwise with pole budget2epsilon. Then w_i(x)<=sup_L w_i+4epsilon M. Nested compact superlevel sets imply sup_L w_i decreases to sup_L v, even if the latter is −infinity; no Dini-to-usc claim is needed. Passing i then epsilon to zero proves v(x)<=sup_L v. This last LIMIT hull comparison retains its unproved controlled-approximation antecedent.

Proofs are in P16.1-argument.md Sections3–5 and P16.1-paper.tex/P16.1-paper.pdf. Rerun python3 rerun.py. finite-checks.json records exact finite diagnostics:504 multinomial grid cases and540 real-support monotonicity cases, plus pole examples. They do not certify the universal proofs. Source Wu2609.27610v1 LF645–707,762–774,1838–1890,1963–2044 is diagnostic; its text hash is c8ffe91a631da67f6d3872a1a06ab8d15755aed2f926cdf326725ca3662cef7d. These new drafts do not establish the original equation.

notes.summary: Repaired split-piece Runge theorem is proved conditionally, with preserved hull neighborhoods, one witness, whole-base trace continuity and gamma=1. Strict Hartogs radii and finite projections are independently reconstructed; analytic gates remain unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: The conditional proof localizes the integer trace only near the tested fiber and puts the closure of every later boundary set inside that preimage. Both K∩Z and K\Z have uniform negative trace bounds. Proper-witness gluing and source generators are retained. Runge is required before coefficient radius calculations. The finite projection treats all separable residue conjugates and proves local isomorphism by the finite cokernel Nakayama argument. Descending reduced strata and final empty-Z globalization are conditional on the explicit metric, controlled, smooth and trace antecedents; they do not yet prove singular EP.
notes.text:
Conditional reconstruction using n1 and n2, not acceptance of the embedded round70 or round79 proofs. Work over countable algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero k. Required analytic antecedents: (A) an actual AFS reference admits an ample rational compactification on the original affine chart; continuous rational contact compact perturbations and whole-collar glued metrics are genuinely PSH and AFS-regularizable; controlled approximation in n2's exact form, genuine decreasing closure and already-genuine same-class sequential regularization with section/generator conversion hold; (B) smooth weak upper-growth regularization and principal-open removal hold, including value equality on the original witness; (C) for each finite map pi:Y→S, Y integral affine and S smooth affine open in A^n, the genuine trace is regularizable for every weak upper-growth input with one witness. Its weights m_y(s) are input-independent positive INTEGERS summing to generic degree d at every analytic fiber; on AFS tests the trace is the whole-base continuous extended determinant norm; boundary radial identification over all completed residue fields is available. These complete antecedents are NOT proved anew in this deliverable.

Under A, Rossi's boundary lemma says x in hull_Y(L)\L and relatively compact open B about x disjoint from L imply x in hull_Y(partial B∩hull_Y(L)). Its continuous compact-perturbation proof separates the compact bad boundary by finitely many original polynomials, adds generator bounds to an AFS function zero on the hull and positive there, multiplies it until it wins over the separating logarithm on the whole boundary, glues the maximum inside B and the reference outside through a whole collar, then uses a uniformly accurate AFS approximant on the compact hull to contradict the hull inequality. This does not assume weak singular regularization.

Let u be weak upper-growth and ORIGINAL u already locally regularizable on affine opens covering Y\Z. With rho from n2, the localized implication is (u+c rho)(x)<=sup_L(u+c rho) for x in hull_Y(L)\Z. If it fails, add a small rational epsilon times v=max_i log|f_i| for ideal generators of Z. Individual floors regularize v with pole set Z. This perturbed usc function attains a finite maximum at y outside L∪Z. Choose B with closure in one principal regularization chart, disjoint from L, and replace rho by n2's support bump rho-prime. The sum q=u+c rho-prime+epsilon v is regularizable there by the ORIGINAL-u hypothesis and has a strict boundary gap c times the bump gap. Rossi and n2's controlled limit hull comparison contradict it. A hypothesis only about u+c rho would not permit subtracting c rho.

Assume pi|Z is a closed immersion and Z-prime=pi^(−1)pi(Z)\Z is closed disjoint from Z. If {u+c rho<0} is not Runge, select compact L within it; normalize the finite hull maximum to zero at x, and choose rational delta>0 with sup_L(u+c rho)<=−delta. The localized implication forces x into Z. The polynomial hull C of {pi(x)} lies in pi(Z) because every polynomial vanishing on that image vanishes on C. Its preimage has disjoint compact pieces in Z and Z-prime. Disjoint neighborhoods A1,A2 avoid the opposite closed pieces; proper closedness gives an initial base neighborhood A of C whose preimage is in their union.

Choose finitely many polynomial constraints with STRICT margins on C, including generator bounds, whose compact closed intersection Q lies in A. Their rational margin normalization gives actual AFS g>=0 with Q={g<=1} and g=0 on an open U about C. Keep this original g,Q,A fixed. Put W={g<1}, W_i=pi^(−1)W∩A_i, open with compact closures. Let h=1 on W1 and0 on W2, and glue h-tilde=max(3g∘pi−1,h) on pi^(−1)W and 3g∘pi−1 elsewhere. The outer reference wins for g>2/3, a whole collar. A gives continuous genuine AFS approximants.

Whole-base trace continuity follows from C, not from continuity on a flat open. On any compact base neighborhood E, decreasing continuous approximants converge uniformly on compact pi^(−1)E, and positivity plus total degree gives ||N a−N b||_E<=d||a−b||_pi^(−1)E. Every AFS trace is continuous by its extended determinant formula, so their locally uniform limit is continuous everywhere. On U this trace is the integer sum of W1 weights, hence LOCALLY constant. Choose O about pi(x) where it equals gamma; do not claim constancy on disconnected U.

If gamma>1, usc supplies a neighborhood N of x in W1 on which u+c rho<delta/[2(gamma−1)]. The W1 fiber at pi(x) is only x, since A1 avoids Z-prime. W1 is clopen in pi^(−1)O; proper closedness shrinks O to O-prime so its ENTIRE W1 preimage is in N. If gamma=1 omit this estimate. Choose B with compact closure inside W1∩pi^(−1)O-prime, disjoint from L. Consequently K=partial B∩hull_Y(L) and EVERY W1 point in its base fibers lie in the same shrunk region with that fixed gamma. The original gluing neighborhoods and polynomial hull neighborhood remain unchanged.

Use rho-prime from n2 at x in B and u-prime=u+c rho-prime. It equals0 at x and is <=−e-prime on K, e-prime>0 INCLUDING c. On W1 let v=u-prime, on W2 let v=0. Choose rational C0>sup_pi^(−1)Q max(u-prime,0)+delta+1 and glue v-tilde=max(C0g∘pi−delta,v) on pi^(−1)W, the reference outside. A whole collar before g=1 is reference-winning. Weak membership is proved on the SINGLE ORIGINAL proper witness for u: pull back rho-prime and g, form the maxima on its two disjoint pieces and glue where they agree with the reference. No unrelated witnesses are glued. The floor ensures generic finiteness; the displayed bound gives upper growth.

On O-prime preimages v-tilde=max(u-prime,−delta) on W1, zero on W2. Trace C makes w=N v-tilde regularizable on S. Its finite pullback retains genuine source generators: for a monic integral equation z^m+sum_{i<m}b_i z^i=0, log|z|<=max_i log|b_i|/(m−i). Polynomial degree bounds and base AFS generator lower growth permit low positive source-generator branches to be appended without changing each pulled AFS function. Rossi gives x in hull_Y(K); actual decreasing AFS hull inequalities give 0=w(pi(x))<=sup_K w∘pi.

For y in K∩Z the W1 fiber is the singleton y of weight gamma, so its trace is <=−gamma min(delta,e-prime). For y in K\Z, the ORIGINAL localized implication yields u-prime(y)<=−delta. Its own positive weight contributes at most −delta. If gamma>1 the other W1 weights total at most gamma−1 and their values are <delta/[2(gamma−1)], while W2 contributes0, so trace<=−delta/2. If gamma=1 there is NO other positive-weight W1 point, so trace<=−delta. These are uniform negative bounds on both compact pieces, contradicting the hull inequality. Thus the split-piece conclusion holds under A–C. With rho>=0, rational c decreasing to0 gives an increasing union of Runge sublevels equal to {u<0}; every compact is in one member, so the union is Runge.

Independently, on an ALREADY RUNGE open D in (Y×A1)^an containing the zero section, countability gives a compact exhaustion. Compact hulls lie in D; polynomial separation from the bad complement in larger generator boxes gives an increasing exhaustion by STRICT polynomial opens Q_i={|g_ij|<exp(b_ij)} with compact closed bounds in D, each preceding bound strictly inside the next. Include base generators and w. For g_ij=sum_l f_ijl(y)w^l, at (y,0) in Q_i the exact disk radius obeys −log d_Qi(y)=max_{j,l>=1}(log|f_ijl(y)|−b_ij)/l. Constant coefficients satisfy strict constraints; every fiber disk obeys the weighted Gauss bound, and Gauss points at all positive radii over H(y) test the converse. The w bound gives a finite floor; on a common compact base box dominated generator branches give local AFS expressions. A closed disk with radius r<d_D(y) is compact in D and hence in one Q_i, so these expressions decrease to −log d_D, including −infinity. Runge precedes this calculation. Interior{|1|<=1}=whole space whereas {|1|<1}=empty disproves the printed weak-interior identity.

Independently, the finite projection lemma is valid over any infinite characteristic-zero K. Compactify integral affine n-dimensional Y in P^d, d>n, and enlarge the reduced closure of a proper closed Z, smooth at closed z, by the boundary. At EACH finite separable residue conjugate of z, avoid secant lines to this enlarged set and tangent directions; their closures have dimension at most dim Z-enlarged+1<=n<d. Avoid also X and lines between conjugates. Their finite invariant union is proper and descends to K; an infinite field has a rational center outside it. Projection is finite: a positive-dimensional line fiber would contain its center in X. The restriction to the enlarged set has a singleton reduced geometric fiber and injective tangent map. At its finite local image algebra A→B, tangent injectivity gives m_B=m_A B+m_B^2; Nakayama gives m_B=m_A B, hence the fiber is its residue field. Distinct conjugate images preclude residue collapse. The finite cokernel B/A has zero fiber, so Nakayama gives (B/A)_mA=0 and a local isomorphism to the SCHEME IMAGE. Iterate to P^n, remove the closed boundary image, choose an affine target S inside a standard A^n chart and restrict the source to the ACTUAL pi^(−1)S, not a larger preimage. This yields a finite surjection with Z restriction a closed immersion.

With A–C, the descending reduced sets Z_{j+1}=Z_j∩closure(pi^(−1)pi(Z_j)\Z_j) have strictly decreasing dimension: maximal-dimensional Z_j components are components of the finite preimage and are absent from the closure of the complementary components. Outside pi^(−1)pi(Z_{j+1}) the split pieces are closed disjoint; apply the product split theorem and Hartogs conversion on actual affine base preimages. Points over pi(Z_{j+1}) outside Z_{j+1} are outside original Z by injectivity, retaining the original local hypothesis. Successive REDUCED singular strata also terminate. The smooth stratum uses B, each next smooth stratum the proved projection lemma. Finally Z=empty gives the global sublevel Runge property, and the product Hartogs conversion gives global regularization. Conversion first forms max(u−2H,M) on a common box where u−2H<=−H; nested compact superlevel sets supply a whole eventual winning collar for the continuous radius approximants. A gives genuine same-ample-class membership BEFORE sequential regularization. These inductions are conditional, not the missing EP theorem.

Projective weak/genuine equality then follows conditionally from actual ample chart weights rho_i, damping by (c−1)rho_i, whole boundary collars, max_i(−rho_i)=0 and class closure as c decreases to1. Countable singular EP still requires resolved-nef connected-fiber constancy and divisorial usc descent. Arbitrary cardinality further requires finite-data descent, actual relative generic-fiber closure and positive MA base change; only individual finite PL/model competitors descend to larger countable fields. With orthogonality and positive pushforward, their contact support and genuine domination would prove the large-field envelope; arbitrary competitors do not descend together. Onto normalization needs TARGET-side approaching EP in BJ5.13 before transporting E1 and measures.

Complete conditional arguments and their exact limits: P16.1-argument.md Sections6–8 and P16.1-paper.tex/P16.1-paper.pdf. notes.summary: Partial paper and rerunnable implementation delivered; candidate=false. The independent metric/smooth/trace gates, countable singular EP and arbitrary-cardinality equation remain unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: New unconditional draft results and conditional Runge improvements are n1–n3. The printed lower-growth smooth affine theorem has a counterexample, without refuting a corrected upper-growth or final singular EP theorem. All original hypotheses and completion criteria remain unchanged. Input preservation, primary hashes, literal units,2651 finite cases and both TeX passes are execution evidence only.
notes.text:
The original P16.1 remains unresolved. The target still covers every reduced irreducible geometrically unibranch projective X over every algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero k, every ample L and dimension, and arbitrary-support intrinsic finite-dual-energy raw targets of mass V.
